topics: Hosting mode decision (Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-27
Start time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Amrita Singh (Kelvin Head of ML), David Park (Kelvin Infra), Rafael Ortega (Kelvin PM)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — Maya here, I'll be your AE during activation and this is Liam our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Amrita Singh: Hi all, Amrita. Sorry, ran a tad late, had a standup.
[00:12] Liam Ortiz: No worries. David, Rafael, thanks for carving out time.
[00:18] David Park: hey — David here. excited to move forward, we wanted to make sure our networking plan works with kelvin's hybrid infra.
[00:25] Rafael Ortega: Rafael — i'll be owning acceptance criteria and timeline on our side.

[00:35] Maya: agenda for today — quick handoff from sales, go over hosting options and recommended path, walk network/security checklist, confirm pilot scope and next steps. expected about 45-60 minutes.
[00:47] Amrita: sounds good. our preference is low latency for inference, but cost matters — we are leaning towards dedicated capacity if the numbers make sense.

[01:02] Liam: good, thanks. just to set expectations: Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation — usually the best tradeoff for production models with steady traffic. Hosted API is fastest to start and cheaper for spiky workloads. Private (VPC) gives you full control for compliance.
[01:20] Rafael: one question — can dedicated run inside our VPC or does it always sit on Redwood-managed network?
[01:28] Maya: great question. Dedicated is a reserved pool we manage, but we support VPC peering for Private deployments. for Dedicated you can choose a dedicated tenancy with tenancy isolation and private endpoint options; if you need a private control plane with customer-managed networking that's Private deployment. Liam — do you want to add the nuance?
[01:45] Liam: yeah. TL;DR: Dedicated (Redwood-managed infra) + Private endpoints: we can provide private endpoint access so traffic doesn't traverse public internet, but the control plane remains hosted unless you opt for Private deployment package. if you need on-prem or air-gapped, that's the Private option. also bandwidth and egress rules will matter for throughput and cost.

[02:15] David: okay, so our ask: we want dedicated throughput, private endpoints (peered), and KMS integration for keys. we also need audit logs going to our SIEM.
[02:25] Maya: perfectly reasonable. We do SOC2 and can integrate with your KMS via customer-managed keys; audit logs can be streamed to your logging endpoint. i'll attach security pack after the call.
[02:36] Amrita: can you confirm tokenization handling and whether there's any PII masking in transit?
[02:42] Liam: Redwood's in-transit is TLS, at rest we can do customer-managed KMS keys. PII masking isn't automatic — that's typically done client-side or via preprocessors. we can recommend middleware patterns (we have a sample lambda to strip/replace pii). i'll share the sample.

[03:05] Rafael: ecosystem question — we're evaluating Anthropic and Vertex for certain workloads. what is Redwood's differentiation from those?
[03:12] Maya: short answer: production-first inference controls and unified runtime across modes. you'll get batching, KV/prefix caching, routing rules, and cost-tuning levers tied to observed token economics. not a model marketplace pitch, more about predictable inference economics. also we surface per-route token and latency breakdowns in the console.
[03:34] Amrita: that's helpful. can the console show token costs per prompt or per-route?
[03:39] Liam: yes — the console gives token-level cost and latency breakdowns, and you can bind alerting to regressions for a prompt set. small caveat — cost attribution for very short sessions can be noisy but the aggregate is solid.

[04:00] [04:00] (brief cross talk)
[04:10] Maya: okay network specifics — David, you mentioned peering. do you have a preferred cloud region and team that handles VPC peering?
[04:18] David: we are in AWS us-west-2. infra team owns peering and we use Transit Gateway. also we have strict egress rules and a proxy.
[04:26] Liam: perfect. we'll need the VPC CIDRs, the list of subnets for endpoints, and any proxy/FW rules that might strip large streaming connections. streaming can require tweaks to idle timeouts.
[04:39] David: noted. proxy idle timeout is 60s right now, could be a problem for longer streams.
[04:44] Maya: that'll need to be raised or we'll use chunked responses to keep connection alive. i'll flag that in the runbook.

[05:02] Amrita: pilot scope — we want to run a 2-week pilot with our standard LLM (finetuned Llama variant) for mainly customer support augmentation. target SLO is 200ms p95 for short responses, 600ms p95 for multi-turn longer replies. is that realistic?
[05:24] Liam: depends on model size and seq length. for a 7B finetuned model quantized to int8 on Dedicated you can hit those numbers with proper batching disabled for low-latency routes. we'll need your average prompt lengths and concurrency.
[05:38] Amrita: estimated concurrent users: 80 peak, average prompt tokens ~120, response tokens ~60.
[05:45] Liam: ok those numbers help. we'll recommend a configuration and run a benchmark. for the latency SLOs, we might suggest hot KV cache enabled for common prefixes to shave ~50-100ms.

[06:05] Rafael: about data retention: we need a 30-day retention policy in transit for logs and no model training on our data.
[06:11] Maya: Redwood does not train models on customer data. logs/inputs retention window is configurable; we'll set the default per your policy and we'll show how to purge logs.

[06:27] [06:27] (brief pause while Maya shares link in chat)
[06:33] Maya: sending runbook link: https://redwood.co/onboarding/runbook/kelvin-draft — note: internal link for review; i'll attach a public copy in follow-up.
[06:45] David: great. Rafael — i'll work with Liam on network config once he shares specifics.

[07:00] Liam: i'll need sample prompts and a traffic trace for the week — even a synthetic trace is fine. can you upload them to the bucket we shared?
[07:09] Amrita: yes, we'll package it. likely by Tuesday.
[07:14] Rafael: timeline question: how soon can we go from pilot to ga if the pilot is successful?
[07:19] Maya: typical runway is 4–6 weeks post-pilot for Dedicated with capacity adjustments and rollout windows, but it can be faster if infra signoff is quick.
[07:28] Amrita: any blockers we should anticipate?
[07:31] Liam: the usual: VPC peering and proxy timeouts, KMS approvals (sometimes takes a few business days), and model variant compatibility for quantization. also quota provisioning on GPUs if you need burst.

[07:50] [07:50] (50s mark — speaker change)
[07:55] David: on KMS approvals — we need a security contact at Redwood and an estimated timing.
[07:59] Maya: i'll include Redwood security contact in the security pack. KMS setup often takes 2–5 business days depending on your cloud policy.

[08:10] Rafael: curious about cost run-rate for Dedicated vs Hosted — can you provide a rough delta?
[08:16] Maya: yes — i'll attach a pricing matrix. ballpark: Dedicated is higher baseline but lower per-token for steady load; Hosted is lower start-up cost for spikey loads. we'll put your numbers into a simple TCO calc.
[08:29] Amrita: also want to confirm SSO and RBAC — we use Okta.
[08:34] Liam: Okta SAML SSO is supported; we also provide granular RBAC for token-scoped roles and route-level controls.

[09:00] Maya: action items recap: i'll send runbook/security pack/pricing matrix; Liam will own benchmark scheduling and test vectors; David will share network details and security contact; Rafael will draft pilot acceptance criteria and share.
[09:15] David: sounds good. one more thing — do you have any references of similar fintech-ish customers running low-latency support?
[09:22] Maya: yes — i can share a short case study (masked) about a payments company that ran a Dedicated pilot — i'll drop that in the follow-up.

[09:36] Amrita: any technical caveats about finetuned llama variants? we've seen differences in KV cache behavior.
[09:42] Liam: some finetunes change tokenization slightly; we test for kv cache hit rate degradation. if you can give us a sample finetuned artifact or a deterministic prompt set we can run preflight checks.

[10:00] [10:00] (quick procedural notes)
[10:07] Rafael: Acceptance criteria draft — we'll aim for: 1) p95 latency targets hit in benchmark window, 2) error rate <0.5%, 3) logs & KMS integration validated. any additions?
[10:18] Liam: also include throughput targets (concurrency) and model output quality checks for a small eval set.

[10:30] Maya: ok — if there's no more major questions i'll summarize next steps and close out.
[10:36] Amrita: one last ask: can Redwood provide a short runbook section for emergency fallback (if Dedicated cluster fails)?
[10:43] Liam: yes — we have an automatic fallback policy to a smaller hosted variant and a canary rollout path; i'll include an example policy.

[10:55] Maya: great. we'll send the follow-up with runbook, security pack, pricing table, and a calendar invite for the benchmark slot. thanks all.
[11:03] David: thanks. looking forward.
[11:06] Amrita: thanks everyone.
[11:08] Rafael: thanks — bye.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription quality: speaker attribution occasionally generalized, some product names slightly misspelled (e.g., Redwood Dedicate), timestamps approximate.
